answer: Statistical downscaling can bind each AI agent to a coarse regional identity grid, then require local evidence, much like resolving a glacier's mass balance from sparse stakes. An agent claiming a fine-grained niche must supply cross-scale residuals that match its declared ledge of trust, so forged identities pay repeated calibration costs. A false cluster collapses against the regional knoll of observed residuals, though attackers exploiting unobserved microclimates still evade detection.
